# Review, pass 1 — secret-history-211-213 (§§211–213)

Reviewer: strongest model, adversarial. Files read: conventions.md, runbook.md, run3/RUNBOOK.md (Reviewer), packet.md, units.json, known-forms.json, novel-forms.json, the model 01-06, and the published parts 093-099, 115-124, 191-193, 202-210 for house renderings. No modern translation opened or recalled. `units.json` edited in place by script; `t` untouched.

## Integrity checks (all clean)
- 40 units consume packet indices 0–236 exactly once, in order; every `t` equals the packet's romanized words joined by single spaces; every `words` list has one entry per word; `ln` 211/212/213 correct; `p: true` on U0 (§211), U10 (§212), U17 (§213) only.
- Every morph's last bracketed Ming gloss was compared with the packet gloss for that word: all agree (the only differences are Ming characters repeated on a stem and its suffix, e.g. 一同 on both töreküi and -lüġe, 也者︀ on both stem and -že, which is acceptable). No Ming gloss invented or misplaced.
- Quote marks: every Shiratori `"` is matched by a curly pair in `i`; the omitted opening mark at U37 is supplied in `i` only and the note says so (U37). Speech spans U1–U8, U11–U15, U18–U23, U25, U26, U27, U30–U35, U37–U38 close correctly.

## Changes (unit · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

1. U18 · i, n, morph · **major** · `i` read "Mönggetü-Kiyan's son, of the three Toquraud and five Tarqud", making the son a member of the three Toqura'ud and five Tarqud; the Mongol (γurban Toquraγ̇ud, tabun Tarqud, Möṅgetü-Kijan-u köġü) is a list, and the plural `ta` of U19 can only be taking the whole company up. The note admitted the grouping was a guess from nothing. The published §§115–120 shows exactly this company arriving together (three Toqura'un, five Tarqud, Möngetü-Kiyan's son with the Bishi'ud and Baja'ud). Also "Toquraud" broke the house γ̇ → ' rule and "Mönggetü" differs from the published "Möngetü". · `i` now "The three Toqura'ud, the five Tarqud, Möngetü-Kiyan's son,"; note rewritten (list in apposition, cites §§115–120, says it is a reading); morph glosses of Toquraγ̇ud and Möṅgetü-Kijan respelled.
2. U19 · i, n · moderate · follows from 1: `ta` is plural, and `i` "you formed" hid that it takes up the whole list; note said the plural subject was "Önggür and his people". · `i` "you all formed"; note now says the subject is the company of U18 with Önggür in apposition.
3. U1 · n · moderate · "Žarčiγ̇udai is the smith-father of Jelme": "smith" is not in the Mongol or the Ming (bellows only), "father" came from nowhere in the note. · Rewritten: Jelme's father on the evidence of §§93–99 (where he leads his son Jelme to Chinggis); kürege is the bellows.
4. U1 · n · moderate · described the Ming 自的行 on ölegei-te-eče as "cradle … from", though 自的 is the Ming's reflexive "own" (as on kürege-ben) and 行 its case mark; the "from" is in the form (-eče), not in the Ming. · Note corrected to say what the Ming has and that the reflexive is not visible in the form.
5. U8 · i, n · moderate · `l` "if-incurring" / note "incur a penalty", but `i` "if he offends … brought to guilt for it" is a different verb and invents "for it"; the published §§202–203, 204–207 (Ming 罰) read alda- as "incur a penalty / be punished". · `i` now "if he incurs a penalty nine times, let him not be brought into guilt."; note cross-refers to the two published uses.
6. U14 · n · moderate · wrong label: öġer-ün glossed "ablative-genitive -ün"; -ün after r is the genitive (the morph already says so). · Corrected to "genitive -ün after r".
7. U31, U32 · n · moderate · dutaγ̇ulun is a converb (-un), "not letting lack", and leads to the conditional of U33; `i` renders it as an imperative without saying so. · Imperative kept in `i` (reads well; the sentence amounts to one) but both notes now say the converb has been turned into an imperative.
8. U33 · n · moderate · -i on qojar and the Ming 兩箇行 point to an object or dative, yet `i` makes "you two" the subject; the note only said the Ming "glosses like a dative". · Note now states the mismatch, offers "if (one) has you two give out" as the alternative, and says the subject reading is a choice. `i` unchanged.
9. U34 · n · moderate · "The idiom is that a host who feeds all his guests has an easy mind": no idiom is shown by the Mongol or the Ming; asserted from outside the text. · Replaced by a statement of the sense that the words themselves bear.
10. U38 · n · moderate · "the Ming implies Tolun's group, not Önggür and Boroqul": the Ming (人名等 一同 / 面北居中 / 敎坐者︀) implies neither. · Reworded: nobody is named; may mean "sit in the middle together with Tolun and the others".
11. U39 · i, n · moderate · `i` "told them their seats and assigned them" doubled the two verbs and added "assigned them"; conventions fix ögbe after a converb tentatively as "did for (me)". · `i` "So saying, he announced the seats for them."; note cites the house pattern.
12. U4 · morph, n · minor · note said stem nököče- + -šeġer, morph said nököčeg- + -šeġer (and the letters do not split as the note said); the published §§204–207 lemma is nököče-. · Morph now nököče- + -gšeġer (both marked uncertain), note matches.
13. U1 · n · minor · "no verb until büleġei, three units on": it is two units on (U1 → U3). · Fixed.
14. U1 · i · minor · -ben is the reflexive-possessive; `l` has "his-own", `i` had "his bellows" (published 093-099: "his own bellows"). · `i` "his own bellows".
15. U2 · n · minor · the genitive on Onan-(n)u was left unexplained (flag-first rule). · Sentence added.
16. U6 · n · minor · "Four forms in a parallel pair" — they are two pairs. · Fixed.
17. U10 · n · minor · Tolun identified with §213's Tolun only by name; the published §§191–193 already lists Tolun-Čerbi. · Note cites it, still marked as an identification.
18. U12 · i · minor · `l` "single wing" but `i` "a wing apart"; the note says "apart" is a guess for öröle. · `i` "a single wing, apart from your father,".
19. U15 · i · minor · "stay and consult" made aqu a separate verb against the house treatment of converb + aqu (§§208–210) and the house "counsel" for eje. · "Will you not stay on, taking counsel with Turuqan?"

21. U37 · l, n · minor · `l` "feast", `i` and morph "banquet"; note "wine bureau" vs morph "wine office". · `l` and note aligned to "banquet" / "wine office".
22. U0, U17, U19, U20, U24, U30, U35 · l · minor · conventions: Shiratori's form of proper names in `l`; the draft had Jelme, Önggür, Boroqul in `l` beside Želme elsewhere in the same `l`. · Želme, Öṅgür, Boroγ̇ul throughout `l` (Chinggis Qaγan kept, as in every published `l`).
23. all units · l, i, n, morph · minor · curly apostrophes and single quotes (Baja'ud, Želme's, ‘to’) against the published parts' straight ' (curly double quotes kept for speech). · Normalised by script; `t` not touched.

## Findings considered and refused
- U3 `i` "he gave me" beside U2 "they came down": the subject of the chain is Jarchiudai, who leads his son (§§93–99) and comes with him; "they" for the arrival and "he" for the giver of the sable swaddling-cloth is defensible, and the note already says "he" is inferred.
- U2 note "Ming 行, 'to'" on the ablative Burqan-Qaldun-ača: the Ming does use 行 on ablatives (ečige-dēče 父行), and the note already says the form is followed.
- U11 `i` as a question: the note records that question versus statement is uncertain; the Ming 怎 supports the question and the choice is declared.
- U6 `i` "Born together at birth, grown together at growth": awkward but faithful to the Ming 生時 一同; a smoother version needs "we", which the note rightly avoids.
- U22 "you went on": jabuba-že with Ming 行了 is "went"; "went on" is a figure for sharing hardship and is flagged in the note. Left.
- U35 converbs morilažu jabužu rendered "mount, go about": the final verb is a plural imperative, and the house chain rule is kept by the note; left.
- U30 cooks "of the right side and the left": the note says the pairing is a reading and U31–U32 use the sides for diners; the Mongol is a bare list, left as declared.
- U37 "At the seating": saγ̇uri saγ̇urun "(at) sitting in the seat" is rendered loosely but the unit is flagged "very uncertain"; left.
- Morph baγ̇urči + -n "plural (Ming 每)" (U30): not in known-forms, but the Ming 每 is the plural mark and the glosser will see baγ̇určin as a token; left.
- `about`: "the rewards of 1206" matches §§204–207 and §§208–210 abouts; left.

## Counts
critical 0 · major 1 (item 1) · moderate 10 (items 2–11) · minor 12 (items 12–23); 23 changes in all.

## Remaining doubts (for pass 2 / the owner)
- U18–U19: the apposition reading of the list and "you all" rests on the plural `ta` and §§115–120, not on the Ming.
- U33: whether "ta qojar-i … tügeġeġeü" has "you two" as subject or object; -ġeü itself.
- U12–U14 (öröle, žiġür, žüġegsen(i)-jer(i)-jen): the "wing" figure and the heavy suffix chain are tentative as the notes say.
- U8: "nine times" — penalties incurred, not offences forgiven; matches the published parts but the Ming is thin.
- Glossary (pass 2): qari needs broadening to "tribe" (Ming 部落, known entry has 邦); köiten "cold" already broadened; tüblen, tüsürge, basaγ̇alažu, eteġed are new and uncertain.

# Pass 2 — secret-history-211-213

Reviewer pass 2. Re-read conventions.md, runbook.md, pass 1, packet.md, known-forms.json, novel-forms.json, units.json, gloss.json; compared the published §§093-099 and 115-120 for the cross-references. No modern translation opened or recalled. Checked by script: 237 packet words = 237 `words` entries, every `t` word equals the packet word; every glossary token of `t` has an entry (gloss.json or known-forms.json), no unused key, no key in both; every `__broaden__` key is a known form and begins with the old entry whole; every Ming gloss of the packet is present in the brackets of its word's morphs (one gap, below). `t` untouched.

## Changes (unit/entry · severity · what was wrong · what was done)
1. gloss `dutaγ̇ulun` + U31, U32 morph and U31 note · **moderate** · glosser/drafter analysed the word as dut- + causative -aγ̇ul- + -un. The Han (都塔兀侖: du-ta-'u-lun) gives duta- + causative -γ̇ul- + converb -un; "dut-" is a modern truncation. · Lemma `duta-`, suffix `-γ̇ul-` in gloss, both morphs and the note.
2. U19 · i, n · moderate · `i` "a Bishi'ud" made Önggür a Bishi'ud; Bišiγ̇ud is a plural (-d) people name, the published §§115-120 has "the Bishi'ud", and Önggür is of the Baja'ud (U25). · `i` "the Bishi'ud"; note says Bišiγ̇ud is a plural people name and that whether Önggür is counted among them is not shown.
3. U18 · n · moderate · pass 1 reported §§115-120 as having "Möngetü-Kiyan's son Önggür with the Bishi'ud and Baja'ud"; the published text has Möngetü, son of Kiyan, with Ünggür and the others, the Bishi'ud, and their Baja'ud. The köġü + (U19) či Öṅgür order also allows "Möngetü-Kiyan's son, you Önggür". · Parallel restated exactly; the alternative named; the plain-list `i` kept.
4. gloss `tara` + U25 morph and note · moderate · entry "tara — dispersed (adjective or converb stem)": the word is the bare stem of tara- "to disperse" (cf. Ming 散), so a verb lemma. · Entry `tara- — to disperse, scatter … (verb stem; uncertain)`; morph lemma `tara-`; note says "I take tara as the bare stem of tara- … cannot analyse bura".
5. gloss `__broaden__` (new) `baγ̇určin` · moderate · known entry is `baγ̇určin — cook [厨子]`, but U30's morph splits baγ̇urči + -n (Ming 厨子每, 每 = plural) and the novel entry is `baγ̇urči`. · Broadened with " · also baγ̇urči with the plural -n, 'cooks' (Ming 厨子每 …)"; morph left as it is.
6. gloss `__broaden__` (new) `mede` · moderate · known entry has only "know!" [知者︀]; here the bare stem has Ming 管 "manage" (U27). · Broadened, old entry whole + " · also Ming 管 'manage' …".
7. gloss `öšküi-lüġe`, U6 morph + note · minor · "participle -küi (written -šküi after s)" is garbled: the š is the stem's s, not part of the suffix. · "the stem's s is printed š before k" in entry, morph and note.
8. gloss `žüġegseni` · minor · carried the Ming of the next word (敎自的(行)) and said "a following -i". · Ming limited to [置來的]; (i) described as Shiratori's bracketed linking vowel, as the note does.
9. U32 `esegsen-e` morph · minor · Ming 不曾的(行): the 的 and 行 stood in no bracket. · -gsen [的], -e [(行)].
10. gloss `töreküi-lüġe` · minor · "together with the being born" ungrammatical English. · "together with being born".
11. gloss `aldaγ̇asu` · minor · Ming 罰 glossed "'punish'"; the notes and §§202-207 say penalty/fine. · "'penalty, fine'".
12. gloss `miṅγa` · minor · bare "thousand" beside known `miṅγan`. · Says it is a short form of miṅγan.
13. gloss `nököčegšeġer`, `qučin` · minor · double or redundant parentheses ("(uncertain) (verb, converb?)", "(verb or noun; uncertain)" after "form and word class uncertain"). · Merged to one grammar parenthesis.

## Checked and left
- All 56 gloss.json entries read against the text, packet and Ming: format, grammar labels (dative-locative, ablative, genitive, comitative, converb of time, optative first/third person, conditional -ġesü/-γ̇asu) and dictionary forms are sound apart from items above. Every entry's first lemma agrees with the morph lemmas of its tokens, except the known `saγu-` (undotted, in the published entry for saγ̇utuγai; unit uses saγ̇u-) and the known `baγ̇určin` (item 5).
- `__broaden__ qari`: begins with the old entry whole, adds Ming 部落 "tribe"; correct.
- Pass-1 edits re-checked (items 1-23): no new error beyond items 2-3 above. Names agree with the house list (Jelme, Önggür, Boroqul, Tolun, cherbi, Qahan; Deligün-Boldaq as in 055-063/093-099); l/i/n use straight ' and curly speech quotes throughout; `l` keeps Shiratori's spellings.
- Not re-opened: pass-1 refusals (all sound).

## Findings considered and refused
- U31 `i` "those who stand, or sit" for baiγsan + saγ̇uγsan-a: dative on the second only is already in the note.
- `soγ̇oṅγuluγ̇asu` lemma `soγ̇oṅγul-` (stem with causative included): analysis unresolvable from the Ming alone, flagged uncertain in entry and note.
- `amuju`, `tüsürge`, `tüblen`, `basaγ̇alažu`, `eteġed`, `žigtü-`: glosser's stems cannot be checked from the text; all are marked uncertain in entry and note, so left.
- `tolun-a` entry's "(probably the Tolun-Čerbi of §§191-193)": an identification in a glossary entry, but marked "probably"; left.

## Counts (pass 2)
critical 0 · major 0 · moderate 6 (items 1-6) · minor 7 (items 7-13); 13 changes.

## Remaining doubts
- U33: subject or object for "ta qojar-i" and -ġeü (unchanged from pass 1).
- U18-U19: whether köġü is Önggür in apposition; whether Önggür is counted among the Bishi'ud.
- Glosser stems resting on the Ming alone: žigtü-, nobši-, köbši-, žüġe-, žiγ̇a-, basaγ̇ala-, tüsürge, tüblen, öröle, bura, qučin, hužaγ̇ur (spelling with h-, as printed).
- Known `saγu-` lemma lacks the dot (published entry, not changed here).
- `dutaγ̇ulun` analysis (item 1) and `tara-` (item 4) rest on the Han syllables and general Mongolian morphology, not on the Ming gloss.
